beats.care: Your canteen thali, onions and cab rides cost more. And loans for bikes, phones or education could get pricier if RBI hikes again in December.
beats.what: Retail inflation hit 5.54% in September, up from 4.83% in August. That is the highest in 23 months.
beats.why: Food prices jumped. Onions more than doubled from a year ago, garlic rose about 55%, and restaurant meals got over 9% costlier.

cards.body: It's the fourth month in a row above RBI's 4% target, and close to its 6% upper limit. Villages are hit harder: rural inflation is 6.08% against 4.88% in cities. Telangana's 6.64% is fourth-highest among big states.

cards.note: Year-on-year price rise. Source: government CPI data via Business Standard.
cards.title: What got pricier in a year (September)

cards.body: When prices keep rising, RBI raises interest rates to cool spending. It hiked to 5.50% this month and expects inflation near 6% from October to December. Many economists expect another hike.
cards.title: why does rbi care about onions?

cards.body: Tomatoes and potatoes are actually cheaper than a year ago, even as onions more than doubled.

opts: Food prices like onions shot up
cards.q: Why did inflation jump in September?
cards.why: Food is a big part of what Indians buy, so when vegetables like onions spike, overall inflation rises fast.

cards.q: Will October's inflation (out mid-Nov) be above 6%?

cover.label: Retail inflation in Sept, a 23-month high

hook: Onion prices *more than doubled* in a year. What else got pricier?

learn.t: Food makes up over a third of India's retail inflation basket, so pricier vegetables quickly push up the overall number.

watch: October's inflation data comes out mid-November. RBI's next rate meeting is 2–4 December, where another hike is widely expected.
